topics.title: Ohm's law
topics.essence: The current through a resistor is proportional to the voltage across it: v = iR. It flows from the higher voltage to the lower.
topics.check: The current through a resistor is zero. What can you say about the voltages at its two ends?

topics.title: KCL
topics.essence: Charge does not pile up at a node. Whatever current flows in must flow out.
topics.check: Three wires meet at a node. Two of them carry 2 mA and 5 mA in. What does the third carry, and which way?

topics.title: KVL
topics.essence: Voltage is a height. Walk around any closed loop and you come back to the height you started at, so the rises equal the drops.
topics.check: A 12 V source drives two resistors in series and one of them drops 9 V. What does the other drop, whatever its resistance?

topics.title: dividers
topics.essence: Series resistors share one current and split the voltage in proportion to R. Parallel resistors share one voltage and split the current in proportion to 1/R.
topics.check: In a two-resistor voltage divider you make the bottom resistor much larger than the top one. Where does the output voltage go?

topics.title: nodal analysis
topics.essence: Name every node voltage, write KCL at each unknown node using Ohm's law, and solve. KVL comes for free.
topics.check: A circuit has four nodes. One is ground and one is pinned by a voltage source. How many equations do you need?

topics.title: phasors & impedance
topics.essence: At one frequency a sinusoid is just an amplitude and a phase, and R, L and C all obey V = ZI.
topics.check: At a very high frequency, does a capacitor look like an open circuit or a short? Say why from Z = 1/(jωC).

topics.title: AC power
topics.essence: Only the part of the current that is in phase with the voltage delivers power on average.
topics.check: The current through a capacitor is a quarter cycle ahead of its voltage. How much power does it take in on average?

links.why: KCL at every unknown node gives Gv = i. Solving the circuit is solving a linear system.
Every voltage in the circuit turns at the same ω, so drop the e^(jωt) and keep the complex number in front.
Average power is ½|V||I|cos φ: half the dot product of the voltage and current phasors.
Reactive power is ½|V||I|sin φ: half their cross product, the part of the current that lies across the voltage.
One loop: the source voltage is shared out across series resistors in proportion to R.
One pair of nodes: the source current is shared out across parallel resistors in proportion to 1/R.
Ohm's law turns each branch current into a difference of node voltages over R.
One KCL equation for each unknown node voltage.
Describing the circuit by node voltages satisfies KVL automatically: every loop already closes.
Impedance is Ohm's law with complex numbers: V = ZI.
Swap each R for a Z and every resistor-circuit method works for R, L and C at one frequency.
Power depends on the angle between the voltage phasor and the current phasor.
Voltage is work per unit charge. Around a closed loop the total work is zero.
